khung k90 năm 1675: [cong_trinh_moc] The Monument column inside the timber scaffolding is a smooth, plain white cylinder. I can't see any fluting on it. — The Monument was built as a fluted Doric column, and in 1675 it was unfinished and still being raised. A smooth, unfluted shaft is the wrong form for it. @px [1018, 421, 1114, 648] tin 0.5

khung k25 năm 1675: [cong_trinh_moc] A tall, slender white tower with a domed or cupola cap and a clock-tower look stands on the skyline at the centre. It rises well above the brick rooftops. — No such tower stood in London in 1675. Old St Paul's was a medieval cathedral with a central tower, and Wren's new cathedral with its dome was not yet built. A smooth white domed tower is an invented or later landmark, and it breaks the 'no dome' condition. @px [1098, 397, 1142, 545] tin 0.6

khung k55 năm 1675: [cong_trinh_moc] A tall, slender white tower stands on the skyline at the centre. It has a rounded, domed cupola top and looks like a minaret or a later clock tower. Nothing like it stood in the City in 1675. — The scene must not show any dome, because the new St Paul's was not yet built. A smooth white tower with a domed cap does not match any London landmark standing in 1675. Old St Paul's stood ruined, and the Wren church steeples were not yet built. @px [1098, 394, 1146, 545] tin 0.5

khung k90 năm 1675: [cong_trinh_moc] A tall, slender, smooth white tower with a small lantern and cupola stands on the skyline in the centre. It looks like a 19th/20th-century clock or campanile tower. — No landmark of this form stood in London in 1675. After the Great Fire, the City's skyline was low brick buildings with a few church steeples. A tower like this is a later addition. (xuất hiện 1850) @px [1098, 400, 1142, 551] tin 0.5
